newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses on Dow coattails, GDP.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses on Dow coattails, GDP.

text.p: Mexican stocks recovered from an early sell-off to close little changed on Monday, as the market took the lead from Wall Street and investors braced for Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting
"Although few expect the Fed to raise interest rates tomorrow, investors are waiting to see just in case," said Hector Jimenez, an analyst at the Inverlat brokerage.
The blue-chip IPC share index closed down 3.73 points, or 0.08 percent, at 4,952.88, after falling 89 points earlier.
"Friday's fall on the Dow Jones had a delayed effect on the bourse today, but we also recovered due to the Dow and today's strong GDP figures," a floor trader said.
The Dow Jones industrial average, meanwhile, rebounded from a low of 7,618.47 points to end up 108.70 points at 7,803.36.
The Finance Ministry announced shortly before trade opened that Mexican gross domestic product rose 8.8 percent in the second quarter from the same quarter last year.

On the broad market, sliders outnumbered gainers by 68 to 22 out of 118 stocks that changed hands. Market caution was clearly visible in wafer-thin trading volume of 56.7 million shares, which was already inflated by a cross trade of 7.5 million shares, dealers said.

Dealing had also slowed on news Alejandro Ortiz, Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz's brother, was shot and killed on Saturday evening. Police said they were investigating a robbery, although no valuables were taken from Ortiz.
"We didn't see it drive the market, but we did get many calls from concerned foreign investors asking what was going on," a floor trader said.

Market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico did most to haul the bourse out of its early slump, ending up 18 centavos (2 cents) at 20.00 pesos ($2.57). The telecommunication company's American Depositary Receipts ended up 1/4 at 51-9/16.

Dealers noted television network TV Azteca, which went public on Friday, recovered from an earlier slump to close unchanged at 36.80 pesos ($4.73) in relatively brisk trade. The stock still ended above its flotation price of 35.43 pesos ($4.56).

Traders said media group Televisa and construction firm Empresas ICA weighed most on the market. Televisa ended off 4.80 pesos (62 cents) at 123.20 ($15.84), while ICA declined 30 centavos (4 cents) to 23.80 pesos ($3.06).
